exposure: Sitting posture achievement (mastering, partially mastering, not mastering unsupported sitting)
Duration of sitting postures (caregiver supported, arms supported, unsupported)
Vocal production (frequency per minute of vocal utterances, vocalizations, babbling, total)
outcome: Communication development (receptive and expressive language skills)
cohort: The study included seventy very preterm infants (gestational age <=32 weeks) with no major brain injuries.
finding: The study found significant positive associations between motor composite score and language scores, and between gross motor and expressive language scaled scores, with infants mastering unsupported sitting showing higher expressive language scores and vocal utterances than those not mastering or partially mastering it.
